chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah and Safwan ibn Yahya from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

If a man performs tawaf between As-Safa and Al-Marwah for nine shawt (paces), he should count one sa'y and discard eight; and if he performs tawaf for eight shawt, he should discard them and restart the sa'y; and if he starts with Al-Marwah, he should discard what he has sa'yed and start with As-Safa. If a man performs sa'y for less than seven shawt, then returns to his family, he must return and complete it, and there is no penalty upon him; and if he did not know what was lacking, he must perform seven sa'y; and if he had already gone to his family or trimmed his nails, he must offer the blood of a cow. Narrated.

key_terms.أَشْوَاطٍ: Shawt (plural of shat, meaning a circuit or pace between the two hills)
key_terms.اَلسَّعْيَ: As-Sa'y (the ritual walking between Safa and Marwah)
key_terms.اَلصَّفَا: As-Safa (one of the two hills between which Sa'y is performed)
key_terms.اَلْمَرْوَةِ: Al-Marwah (the second hill in the Sa'y ritual)
key_terms.دَمُ بَقَرَةٍ: Dam of a cow (the specific expiation sacrifice required for certain errors)
key_terms.قَصَّرَ: Qassara (to trim or cut, specifically referring to trimming nails or hair)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for correcting mistakes in the number of circuits during Sa'y in Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the precise mechanics of *Sa'i* between Safa and Marwa, emphasizing the necessity of seven complete circuits and offering specific remedies for counting errors or premature departure. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between minor omissions, which require completion, and actions like trimming nails that incur a blood sacrifice (*dam*), reflecting the rigorous attention to ritual purity and validity in Al-Tusi's compilation.
